experiment: CG-10 R3 — Whirlpool W11174426 LCX/LCC platform architecture falsification within same manufacturer. Ask which concepts disappear when surface-control architecture changes — NOT whether LCX validates Copernicus.

r3DecisionGate.question: Which apparent Whirlpool concepts disappear when surface-control architecture changes (LCX infinite-switch vs Copernicus ACU relay)?
r3DecisionGate.corpusLimitation: R3 is NOT a third independent manufacturer — document alongside R1/R2. Samsung electric range manual absent from corpus.

power_supply.rationale: 240 VAC prerequisite and terminal-block checks on LCX/LCC — same functional power role as R1/R2.

control_board.rationale: LCX/LCC control board orchestrates oven relay tests and diagnostics entry (CANCEL×2+START). Independent of surface switch implementation.

user_interface.rationale: Keypad P11 harness; F2E1 shorted keypad — UI functional role unchanged across Whirlpool platforms.

temperature_sensor.rationale: RTD 1000–1200 Ω Con3/P3 with F3E0/F6E1 — third independent manual family confirms oven cavity temperature feedback as functional role.

oven_heating_system.rationale: LCX chart lists separate bake and broil element Ω rows — same decomposition posture as R1 Copernicus and R2 LG. Monolithic aggregate not supported.

bake_heating_element.rationale: Dedicated bake element procedure 10–40 Ω — invariant across all three probes.

broil_heating_element.rationale: Dedicated broil element procedure separate from bake on LCX.

convection_heating_element.rationale: No convection element procedure on LCX electric chart — convection fan mentioned in operation notes only. Electric convection element evidenced on R2 LG only.

surface_heating_system.rationale: Cooktop heat generation is a testable functional domain via infinite-switch procedure — but switching mechanism is implementation detail (see surface_control).

surface_heating_element.rationale: LCX tests infinite switches in aggregate — not per-zone element procedures like LG. Physical elements are platform instances; zone granularity is model/overlay scope.

surface_control.rationale: Infinite switch is LCX surface control implementation — NOT a candidate for canonical promotion. Functional invariant is control_board → surface_heating_system (heat generation command path), analogous to compressor_controller on refrigerators.

oven_cavity.rationale: Cavity referenced in convection fan door-interlock notes — no standalone cavity test.

convection_fan.rationale: Manual documents convection fan door-interlock behavior but no dedicated fan procedure on LCX seeds (unlike R1 vent-fan and R2 convection-motor procs).

oven_door_switch.rationale: Door switch logic embedded in latch procedure on LCX (F5E1) — not standalone door-switch proc like R2 LG. Functional door authorization evidenced; test style varies.

door_latch_motor.rationale: Latch motor 500–3000 Ω — self-clean actuator implementation on LCX.

thermal_protection.rationale: F6E1 over-temp routes to oven sensor procedure — no dedicated thermal-fuse proc on LCX (R1 Copernicus has thermal-fuse seed). Protection may be fuse hardware on some platforms, sensor-limited path on others — platform/conditional not canonical.

cooling_fan.rationale: No electronics cooling fan procedure on LCX. R1 combined vent/convection fan; no functional distinction preserved in LCX procedure seeds.

oven_lamp.rationale: No oven lamp procedure on W11174426 electric seeds.

warming_drawer.rationale: Warming drawer not in W11174426 procedure catalog.

platformProbeAnswers.question: Does surface_control remain functional when implementation changes to infinite switches?
platformProbeAnswers.finding: No — infinite_switch is platform implementation on LCX; Copernicus uses ACU relay mediation (R1 bridge-element). Invariant functional relationship: control_board → surface_heating_system (surface heat generation command). Switching mechanism stays platform knowledge — do NOT promote infinite_switch to canonical.

platformProbeAnswers.question: Are individual surface zones still independently testable functions?
platformProbeAnswers.finding: Conditionally — LG R2 decomposes LF/LR/RR/RF/CR zones with separate procedures. LCX R3 tests infinite switches in aggregate (one procedure). Copernicus R1 tests bridge/single elements via ACU relay. Zone independence is instance/overlay scope when OEM provides per-zone tests — not a required canonical split.

platformProbeAnswers.question: Does dedicated thermal-fuse procedure presence make thermal_protection implementation-specific?
platformProbeAnswers.finding: Yes — R1 Copernicus has w11746350-thermal-fuse procedure; R2 LG and R3 LCX route over-temp via oven sensor (F6E1/F-6) without dedicated fuse proc. thermal_protection is better modeled as conditional/platform vocabulary (fuse vs sensor-limited path) than canonical component — analogous to refrigerator conditional concepts.

platformProbeAnswers.question: Does evidence preserve electronics cooling vs oven convection as distinct functions?
platformProbeAnswers.finding: No clear canonical split — R1 combines vent/convection in one procedure; R2 separates convection motor from element; R3 documents convection fan behavior without fan procedure. convection_fan may earn canonical/conditional role when procedure evidence exists; cooling_fan remains deferred (no tri-manual procedure support).

triangulationSynthesis.heatGenerationArchitecture: Functional domain: oven heat generation with bake/broil/convection as instance-scoped diagnostic functions — NOT three canonical component types.
triangulationSynthesis.surfaceArchitecture: Functional domain: surface_heating_system with control→heat invariant; infinite_switch / relay / per-zone elements remain platform.

freezeOutcomeRecommendation.rationale: Functional model holds across Whirlpool Copernicus, LG LRE, and Whirlpool LCX. Refine: reject oven_heating_system aggregate; use instance scopes for bake/broil/convection; keep surface_control and infinite_switch as platform; thermal_protection conditional/platform. Human freeze gate must earn every node.
